_comment: Registration for the HARDCODED_PASSWORD heuristic of lib/security/modules/secrets.py,
and specifically for the shell-substitution exemption added by issue #1717.
WHY IT NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): this module is a detector whose silence is
read as 'no hardcoded password here' by /flow:finish, /flow:deploy and /security:* in
every consumer, and nothing downstream re-derives it. An exemption is the change most
able to make that silence wrong.
WHY A SEPARATE CONTROL. controls/secret-scan guards scripts/secret-scan-check.sh, which
runs gitleaks and never loads this module. controls/lib-security-gate runs the
flow_finish policy, which blocks CRITICAL only, so a HIGH heuristic finding cannot move
its verdict. Neither could notice this exemption widening.
THE INVOCATION imports the module by its dotted name from the tree {gate} sits in, so
the anchor's own small tree substitutes for the real package, and prints POSITIONS
only: a finding's value is never shown.
THE BAD CASE IS THE ONE THE EXEMPTION MUST NOT REACH: a hardcoded fallback inside
${NAME:-...}. The GOOD case holds the three shapes it exists for.
invocation:
import sys, os, importlib; root = sys.argv[1]
for _ in range(4): root = os.path.dirname(root)
sys.path.insert(0, root); mod = importlib.import_module('lib.security.modules.secrets'); result = mod.scan(sys.argv[2])
hits = sorted((f.file_path, f.line_number) for f in result.findings if f.id == 'HARDCODED_PASSWORD')
if not result.units_scanned: print('secret-assignment-shell: UNKNOWN - zero files scanned; unchecked, not clean'); sys.exit(2)
[print(f'HARDCODED_PASSWORD: {path}:{line}') for path, line in hits]
print(f'secret-assignment-shell: {result.units_scanned} file(s) scanned, {len(hits)} hardcoded-password finding(s)'); sys.exit(1 if hits else 0)
unknown_signal: ^secret-assignment-shell: UNKNOWN - zero files scanned; unchecked, not clean$
limits: Covers ONE boundary of the shell-substitution exemption: a default inside ${NAME:-...} is still reported, and the three exempt shapes ($(...) at the start, a bare ${NAME}, exactly $NAME) are not. It does not cover the other operator forms, single quotes, non-shell files, a literal before or after a substitution, a second segment joined on after the closing quote, an apostrophe inside the quotes, an unclosed parenthesis, a second assignment on one line, or the HARDCODED_SECRET pattern - tests/test_security_scanners.py pins each of those before and after. It does not cover the KNOWN MISS: a literal inside a command substitution, password="$(echo a-literal)", is not reported, because the pattern cannot see inside $(...). It says nothing about files with no extension, which this module does not scan at all.

cases.name: bad-fallback-literal
cases.why: db_password="${DB_PASSWORD:-fallback-literal-9x}" in a shell file. The fallback is a literal in the file. If it scores GOOD the exemption has widened from 'is a substitution' to 'starts with one'.

cases.name: good-substitutions
cases.why: $(generate_secret), $pg_password and ${DB_PASSWORD}, each in double quotes in a shell file. No secret is written in the file. Separates a working exemption from one that was removed or never applied.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the plausible wider exemption - any double-quoted value beginning $ in a shell file is treated as a reference. 'Starts with a substitution' mistaken for 'is a substitution'. It reports nothing on cases/bad-fallback-literal.
